summary: Prebuilt Linux binary implements WebRTC-signaled remote PTY agent
details: The package ships a single ~13MB Linux/amd64 Go ELF at bin/sxt and no source. Symbols in the binary show a complete WebRTC peer stack (pion/webrtc v4, pion/ice, pion/dtls v3, pion/sctp, pion/turn v5, pion/datachannel), a websocket client (coder/websocket) for signaling, STUN/TURN traversal, and pty/signal/register/c2 identifiers alongside a QR-code library — the structure of a remote-terminal agent where a remote WebRTC peer drives a local PTY on the host running the binary. The package's only external link is a license URL pointing at github.com/ddos798/claude_control; no sextant-branded homepage, repository, or documentation is present in package metadata. The binary is not auto-executed via npm lifecycle scripts or a main entry, so the remote-PTY channel opens when a user runs bin/sxt; once invoked, a remote party reachable via the signaling/TURN path holds interactive shell-level control of the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
